headline: High: Gemini CLI’s broad filesystem/MCP/write access can conflict with dbt-core’s warehouse-facing workflows, creating default data-leak and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: dbt-core can ingest warehouse data and Gemini CLI can read/write the filesystem and use MCP, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or MCP outputs could be treated as instructions. The pair lacks any documented provenance or isolation mechanism, making prompt injection plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or MCP channel
IF dbt-core parses content from files or warehouse outputs as trusted instructions
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents
Disable MCP for the Gemini CLI session
Require explicit human review of any dbt-generated text before reuse
Use read-only mounts for dbt inputs where possible
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while Gemini CLI can read files, access user-provided directories, and egress broadly to Google APIs. If warehouse-derived artifacts land in the shared filesystem, Gemini CLI can ingest and transmit them, creating a default leakage path even without special configuration.
conditions: IF warehouse data is materialized into files in the shared cwd
IF Gemini CLI is allowed to read those files during a session
mitigations: Keep warehouse outputs out of the shared cwd
Restrict Gemini CLI to a scrubbed directory
Turn off network egress for the Gemini session where feasible
Redact sensitive columns before materialization
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write to the same filesystem, and Gemini CLI can modify git state while dbt-core commonly operates on project files and generated artifacts. The shared-state model explicitly says coordination is via filesystem and git only, so concurrent writes can corrupt work or overwrite changes in default use.
conditions: IF both agents target the same repo or working directory
IF either agent writes generated artifacts or commits without external locking
mitigations: Run each agent in a separate clone
Pause one agent before the other writes
Use git worktrees for isolation
Review diffs before commit or apply
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can act on files and git state, so if it consumes dbt-core outputs as authoritative, errors in dbt artifacts can cascade into edits or commits. dbt-core does not provide a verification layer for Gemini’s downstream actions, so the interaction is risky in default workflows but not inherently irreversible.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI uses dbt-generated artifacts as source-of-truth
IF Gemini CLI is permitted to commit or edit based on those artifacts
mitigations: Require manual verification before git commits
Compare dbt outputs against source models
Limit Gemini CLI to suggestion-only mode
Keep action-taking steps separate from analysis steps
requires-engineering: add schema validation for dbt outputs

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core handles data warehouse data, while Gemini CLI sends prompts to Google APIs and can read local files. If regulated warehouse data is placed into the CLI context, the pair can create a residency or retention mismatch; the profiles do not show a DPA or residency control, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-bound warehouse data is exposed to Gemini CLI
IF the deployment lacks a documented DPA or retention policy alignment
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from CLI prompts
Use synthetic or masked datasets
Confirm vendor retention settings before use
Keep compliance-sensitive workflows in dbt-only paths
requires-engineering: obtain legal/compliance approval and DPA review
